title: Tensor products, scalar extension and stalks of lisse sheaves of modules
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme with a geometric point $\bar y$, and let stalks at $\bar y$ be those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. For a finite ring $\Lambda$ (not necessarily commutative), call a sheaf $\mathcal F$ of left $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] *lisse* if there are an etale covering $\{U_i\to Y\}$ and finite left $\Lambda$-modules $M_i$ with $\mathcal F|_{U_i}\cong\underline{M_i}_{U_i}$ as sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules, where $\underline M$ is the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the constant presheaf $U\mapsto M$.

1. *(Constant sheaves.)* For a ring $\Lambda$ and a $\Lambda$-module $M$, the map $M\to(\underline M)_{\bar y}$ sending $m$ to the germ of the global constant section $m$ is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-modules.
2. *(Tensor products.)* Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative finite ring and $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ lisse sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules. The tensor product $\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G$ (sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal F(U)\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G(U)$) is lisse: on an etale $U$ where $\mathcal F|_U\cong\underline M$ and $\mathcal G|_U\cong\underline N$ one has $(\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G)|_U\cong\underline{M\otimes_\Lambda N}$. The map $\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G_{\bar y}\to(\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G)_{\bar y}$, $s_{\bar y}\otimes t_{\bar y}\mapsto(s\otimes t)_{\bar y}$, is an isomorphism, natural in $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ and compatible with the associativity, commutativity and unit isomorphisms on both sides.
3. *(Scalar extension.)* Let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a homomorphism of finite rings and $\mathcal F$ a lisse sheaf of left $\Lambda$-modules. Then $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F$ (sheafification of $U\mapsto\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F(U)$) is a lisse sheaf of left $\Lambda'$-modules, $(\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F)|_U\cong\underline{\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda M}$ where $\mathcal F|_U\cong\underline M$, and $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F_{\bar y}\to(\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F)_{\bar y}$, $\lambda'\otimes s_{\bar y}\mapsto(\lambda'\otimes s)_{\bar y}$, is an isomorphism of $\Lambda'$-modules, natural in $\mathcal F$ and compatible with composites $\Lambda\to\Lambda'\to\Lambda''$.

proof.text: For the constant-module stalk map, use Point.presheafFiberConstIso in the module category: the constant pointed-neighbourhood diagram has value M and connected index category [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-constant-connected-diagram]. Its coprojection at the terminal neighbourhood is the inverse constant-fibre isomorphism. Naturality of toPresheafFiber identifies the displayed global-section germ with this coprojection followed by presheafFiber.map(toSheafify). The latter map is an isomorphism by the generic point sheafification API [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-geometric-stalk]. This works directly for modules, without forgetting to abelian groups.

proof.text: Tensor lissity follows by combining the existing IsLocallyConstantSheaf.tensorObj_part [lem-weil-pbc-flc-tensor-locally-constant-part] and IsFiniteSheaf.tensorObj_part [lem-weil-pbc-flc-tensor-finite-part]. For the precise local tensor formula, express a tensor of sheaves as sheafification of their sectionwise tensor, using the sheafification counit and its monoidal tensorator. The Over.forget U pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility identifies its restriction with sheafification on the localized site. Tensor the two given local isomorphisms; monoidality of sheafification identifies the tensor of the two constant sheaves with the constant sheaf at M tensor N.

Apply etale_stalk_tensor_unique, etale_stalk_tensor_natural, and the coherence part of etale_stalk_tensor_coherence from [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] to the lisse sheaves. These statements apply without finiteness or lissity hypotheses, so give the required special cases unchanged.

For scalar extension, restriction commutes with sheafification by the same Over.forget U compatibility. The left adjunction ringExtendScalarsAdj implies preservation of sheafification, so presheafToSheafCompComposeAndSheafifyIso identifies the extension of the constant sheaf at M with the constant sheaf at the extended module. Apply these isomorphisms to the given trivializing cover to prove local constancy and to obtain the exact local formula. To prove finite generation of the extended module E(M), take a finite generating set of M and its image under the adjunction unit. If a monomorphism N to E(M) contains these images, pull it back along the unit after restriction of scalars. Finite generation of M makes the projection to M an isomorphism, yielding a lift of the unit to N. Transpose this lift across the adjunction; its composite with N to E(M) is the identity by injectivity of the hom equivalence. Thus the monomorphism is an isomorphism, proving finite generation. At each geometric stalk apply this argument and the canonical presheaf-fibre and sheafification comparison isomorphisms, then the universe-lift stalk isomorphism. This proves scalar-extension lissity, including for noncommutative rings.

proof.text: For scalar stalks, specialize etale_stalk_scalar_component_unique in [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] to ringExtendScalarsAdj. Evaluate its unit equation on a section; S-linearity extends the formula from the unit tensor to b tensor a. Naturality follows by composing the naturality equations of the inverse presheafFiberCompIso and inverse presheafToSheafCompSheafFiberIso. For composites, specialize etale_stalk_scalar_iteration from the same node. The two adjoint-uniqueness associativity isomorphisms agree because their hom-equivalence images agree after composing with the inverse restriction-of-scalars comparison. The unit equation for ringExtensionComp sends the two nested unit images to the composite unit image; linearity gives d tensor (s tensor m) mapping to (d times g(s)) tensor m. Evaluate the iteration theorem section equation on that nested tensor and use naturality of the units to move extension maps through pure tensors. Its stalk equation is exactly the required composite compatibility.

Geometric points have IsAlgClosed fields; stalks are the fibres of (pointSmallEtale y).ulift.{u+1} and the tensor product is Sheaf.monoidalCategory, with the canonical Monoidal fibre instance, exactly as in lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar. Stalk, naturality and coherence clauses carry the lisse hypotheses of the node. Scalar extension is ModuleCat.ringExtendScalars / Sheaf.ringExtendScalars of def-pod-ring-scalar-extension; its stalk comparison is the canonical inverse fibre comparison, pinned by the pure-germ formula b tensor a_y to (b tensor a)_y.
